> 晉。康侯用錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接。

Hexagram 35 is about advancing, and its dictionary entry is the best gloss in the whole book.

## 晉，進也。日出而萬物進

說文: 晉，進也。日出而萬物進 — the sun comes out and the ten thousand things advance.

Six characters, and the subject of the sentence is not a person. It is not "a person moves forward." It is: the sun rises, and everything below it grows.

The bronze form has been read as arrows plus the sun, arrows advancing toward the sun. That is one account and it cannot be settled, so this book records it and does not build on it.

But the first layer already fixes the chapter: 晉's advance is the sun's advance, not a person's contest.

The sun does not compete, and everything grows underneath it.

## 康侯

The first words of the judgement are about a person, and they contain a surprise: 康 is 安 — at ease, at rest.

康侯: the marquis who keeps the people calm, who does not agitate for credit.

So a hexagram named "advance" opens with a lord whose virtue is that he does not push.

## 錫馬蕃庶，晝日三接

錫 is 賜, to bestow. 蕃庶: many. Horses and carriages in abundance.

晝日三接: received three times in a single day — the heaviest honour given to a feudal lord.

So the chapter's picture of advancement is not a climb. It is being met, repeatedly, by the one above.

## 摧如

初六 晉如，摧如，貞吉。罔孚，裕無咎.

摧: to be pressed back, held down. Advancing, and being pushed back.

罔孚: not yet trusted. 裕: at ease, unhurried.

So: advance, be pushed back, and do not rush to be believed. The line's instruction is patience about reception, which is a strange thing to require at the first step of success.

## 愁如 / 介福 / 王母

六二: advancing, and worried.

介福: great blessing. 于其王母 — from the 王母: one reading is the grandmother, another is the sovereign yin (the sixth five, the ruler of the upper trigram).

This book takes the sense of a root: the blessing comes from the base line of the family, not from outside.

Which is the second line's correction to the first: advancement that has a source does not need to be believed by everyone.

## 鼫鼠

九四 晉如鼫鼠，貞厲.

The 五技鼠, as 荀子·勸學 describes it: can fly but not reach the roof, can climb but not to the top of the tree, can swim but not cross the valley, can burrow but not hide itself, can run but not outrun anyone.

Five skills, five failures.

So the picture of the line that advances wrongly is not weakness. It is a surplus of capacities with no single one carried through — many talents, no mastery.

## 失得勿恤

六五 悔亡，失得勿恤，往吉，無不利.

恤: to worry. No longer worrying about loss and gain.

At the ruler's place, in the middle of brightness, the line simply stops keeping score — and the verdict is 往吉，無不利.

## 晉其角

Top line: 晉其角 — advancing to the horn, the tip, the extreme.

And the book notes that 角 is the same character as the ram's horn in 大壯, the previous hexagram: there, an animal's horns caught in a fence; here, a person's advancement reaching its end.

維用伐邑 — it can only be used to punish one's own town. The most advanced position has nothing left to advance toward except its own household, and the verdict is 厲吉，無咎 — dangerous, good, no fault. Which is the most honest description of a career at its ceiling.

## 自昭明德

The 象: 君子以自昭明德 — make one's own bright virtue evident.

昭 is to bring into the light, and the object is 自 — oneself.

Which closes the chapter's argument about advancement: the sun rises and things grow; the person who advances in that manner does not push forward, they make what is already there visible.

## The test

Take a promotion, a launch, or a season of growth you are in. Ask whether the advance is yours or the sun's — that is, whether things grow because you are pushing, or because something you keep rising makes them able to. 康侯 did not push.
